gabor — 2D texture op

• Data kinds: image → image

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "gabor", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

• HALCON equivalent: gen_gabor (the HALCON reference is a useful guide to its meaning and parameters)

*The figure is the actual output on a synthetic 128×128 input. Left: input, right: output. Point clouds are drawn as a top-down scatter (brightness = z), 1-D series as a line plot, volumes as the maximum-intensity projection along z, videos as the middle frame, complex images as magnitude; return values that are not pictures are shown as the values themselves.*

*The output is shown in a viridis-like pseudo-colour (dark purple = low, yellow = high) so that a field of quantities — distance, phase, orientation, depth — can be read.*

Sweeping knob a (0.1 / 0.5 / 0.9, the other knob at its default):

▸ gabor: knob a sweep (docs site)

Sweeping knob b (0.1 / 0.5 / 0.9, the other knob at its default):

▸ gabor: knob b sweep (docs site)

On other images (synthetic scene / photo / coins. Top row: inputs, bottom row: their outputs. Knobs at default):

▸ gabor: other inputs (docs site)

*The 4th column is a colour (H,W,3) input. This op handles colour without crossing channels (it does not convolve the colour channel as a third spatial axis).*

Usage

Gabor energy |v * g| — an oriented band-pass texture response.

• a — orientation θ = π·a [rad]. The kernel's cosine runs along the x direction after rotation, so a=0 (θ=0) responds most strongly to vertical stripes (a pattern whose brightness changes along the column direction), and a=0.5 (θ=90°) responds to horizontal stripes. a=1 is θ=180°, the same orientation as a=0.

• b — spatial frequency 0.1 + 0.3·b [cycles/px].

★Normalisation (fix of 2026-09-02): a fixed scale dividing by the L1 norm of the kernel. Previously it divided by _norm = the maximum absolute value in that image, so the magnitude of the response itself was lost. Measured (horizontal stripes 96×96, frequency 0.25): the mean amplitude of the raw convolution was 0.0165 at θ=0° and 0.9077 at θ=90°, a difference of 54.9 times, yet after _norm the means were squashed to 0.3554 vs 0.4790 = 1.35 times — a feature meant to tell orientations apart had lost its discriminative power (naturally, since each orientation was divided by a different divisor). Since |v| <= 1 implies |v * g| <= sum|g|, dividing by L1 keeps the range [0,1] and gives an absolute scale comparable across ops.

Border handling: mirror repeating the edge pixel (d c b a | a b c d — scipy's default reflect) (measured; tools/impl2/border_probe.py).

Blank frame (measured): feeding an image of uniform brightness gives an empty result — every pixel is background (0) — regardless of the brightness. Pure white and pure black behave alike; brightness by itself detects nothing.
